The Effects of a Consistent Morning Run

This stuck with me after I read it. I'm sure there is lots of literature on what your resting heart rate can tell you, but if your body is functioning on less heart beats per minute, things must be in good condition. If it takes a lot of heart beats per minute just to keep you breathing, that's a bad sign.

I don't have a handy tool to measure mine, but I'm going to do it manually for a while. I'm off track on excercising right now and it will be interesting to see how much it changes as I'm being active daily again. I'm sure my resting heart rate is pretty bad right now.

Heart rate variability is a better indicator. I use Ithlete. However, it does seem to correlate well with RHR. Every time it has told me to take a recovery day, my RHR was also 10 points or so higher than normal.

I think you might be over-doing it, and need to take a day off here and there. Your RHR rising, and your HRV lowering are indicators of over-training. If you don't want to take a day off, go for easy runs, keeping your HR real low (110-120ish) and see how that effects your RHR the next day.

That is why your RHR went down when you took a break.

Dr. Phil Maffetone goes into all of this quite thoroughly, and is an excellent source for understanding your HR and the need for recovery and avoiding over-training.

Good luck.
